hypotheses_validated.claim: Belady (with bypass) as implemented is the exact offline optimum for single-request streams and upper-bounds every online policy on the same trace/budget.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: tests/py/test_sim.py::test_belady_is_exactly_optimal_on_small_streams (40 random streams vs exhaustive search) and test_belady_upper_bounds_every_online_policy (6 cache/spec configs) pass; ran locally.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Global LRU collapses to ~0 hits when the cache is smaller than one token's working set (L_moe*k) under cyclic layer access, while LFU keeps hot experts.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_lru_cyclic_pathology (olmoe shape, 64 slots < 128: LRU < 0.5%, LFU > 20%); SIMULATED kimi-k2 4-8 GiB: LRU 0% vs LFU 22-34%; kimi-k3 on this-pc (1462 slots < 1472 working set): LRU 8% vs LFU 39%.

hypotheses_validated.claim: The stream-dedupe synthetic sampler equals successive sampling (Gumbel-top-k) without replacement.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_synthetic_matches_successive_sampling: max marginal deviation < 0.02 at 30k tokens; ad-hoc check 0.0025-0.006 at 40k tokens.

hypotheses_validated.claim: The simulator meets the speed requirement: 2000-token Kimi-K2 trace through all online policies well under a minute.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Measured on this-pc: 5 online policies 2.7 s total when quiet, 9.6 s at 99% CPU load from other engineers; Belady 0.6-2.6 s.

hypotheses_validated.claim: calibrate() recovers known calibration scalars from (Result, tok/s) points.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_calibrate_recovers_known_scalars: rms log error < 0.01, io_eff within 10%.

hypotheses_validated.claim: tests/py/test_sim.py detects behaviour-changing mutations of the simulator core.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: governance/tools/mutate.py (30 mutants/file, seed 1): cache 86.7%, timing 86.7%, trace 93.3%, core 86.7%; every survivor inspected and equivalent/behaviour-neutral. Mutation testing also exposed a Nelder-Mead stall in calibrate(), fixed with restarts.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Speculative decoding (prompt lookup, batched verification) speeds up storage-bound MoE decode in general.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: SIMULATED kimi-k2/this-pc: k=4 alpha=0.6 gives 0.71x at reuse 0.25; it only helps when consecutive tokens share experts (reuse >= ~0.5 at alpha 0.8, ~0.75 at alpha 0.6) or when DRAM-bound (kimi-k3 workstation 1.70x at alpha 0.8). Verification loads the union of the window's experts.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: LFU with the engine's default decay 0.995 dominates LRU whenever routing is skewed at all.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: SIMULATED kimi-k2/this-pc with cache > per-token working set: at zipf 0 / 0.5 with reuse 0.25, LFU(0.995) hit 12% / 25% vs LRU 31% / 34%; decay 0.9 matches LRU there and stays within 2 points of 0.995 at zipf 1.1.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Next-layer prefetch recovers most storage stall when storage is the bottleneck.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: SIMULATED kimi-k2/this-pc: recall 0.8 gives only 1.14x; 79% of prefetches arrive late because the single drive is saturated by demand reads; prefetch only fills storage idle time during attention.

open_questions: Real routing skew (Zipf exponent) and temporal locality of Kimi/DeepSeek models are unknown until engine traces are recorded; SIMULATED kimi-k2/this-pc spans 0.6-1.7 tok/s over zipf 0-1.4.
Should the engine's default LFU heat decay be ~0.9 instead of 0.995? Needs real traces; hx_store_opts.heat_decay is not exposed in hearth_options.
Real next-layer predictor recall for the engine's two-step ('shared') prefetch; the sim takes recall as an input.
All timing scalars are uncalibrated (overhead 1 ms/step, 20 us/layer, efficiencies 1.0) until T09 fits them with calibrate().
